analyses.failure: test_chk_031_clock_stop_during_srst: AssertionError 'CHK-005: record 17 never sampled' (test_async_gray_fifo.py:1438 -> TB.rec:330)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:959-961 (CHK-031): 'The handshake has no timeout. It waits while a clock is stopped and completes when the clock runs again.' Stimulus: 'pulse i_rst_n_sw low for one cycle. After o_sw_rst_busy=1, stop i_clk_rd for 60 write cycles, then restart it.' Expected: 'While i_clk_rd is stopped: o_sw_rst_busy=1, o_full=1, no write is accepted, and o_overflow=0.' rules.json:6840 AF-10.7.5-09 (CC-09): 'A clock stops during the reset; Behavior: The handshake waits until the clock runs again (DEC-036)'. rules.json:10012 AF-20.1-06 (ASM-006): 'If a clock stops, the handshake waits until it runs again; there is no timeout.'
analyses.rtl_does: No RTL behaviour is involved in this assertion. The message comes from the testbench helper TB.rec (test_async_gray_fifo.py:325-330), not from a DUT check. RTL for reference: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:175-178 holds the FSM in REQ until w_ack_s, so with i_clk_rd stopped busy stays 1 (wr.sv:202,208-213), and o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n = 1 (wr.sv:102,125). Nothing in the log shows the DUT misbehaving during the stop window. The window check at line 1439 never ran.
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:1425-1433: writes 3 words, sets sw=0 at w1, then sw=1, checks busy=1, calls stop_clock(RCLK), sets s0 = tb.wr.n (=17), and does 60 more writes through tb.w. Lines 1434-1438: resume_clock, s1 = tb.wr.n (~77), then for i in range(s0,s1) it calls `await tb.rec(tb.wr, i)`. TB.rec (lines 325-330) is `for _ in range(i - len(mon.trs) + 50): if len(mon.trs) > i: return mon.recs[i]; await mon.tick()` followed by `assert False`. When record i is already more than 50 records old (len(trs) ~77, i=17 gives range(17-77+50) = range(-10)), the loop body never runs. The record exists, but the helper asserts 'never sampled'. Timing confirms this: the test starts at 1354060.82 ns, init ends at 1354197.38 ns, and 65 write ticks of 10 ns later the test fails at 1354839.78 ns (sim.log:449-460). The helper did not wait any extra edges, which matches a zero-iteration loop. The expected values (busy=1, full=1, overflow=0 while i_clk_rd is stopped) come from the contract, but they were never evaluated.

candidates.evidence_for: TB.rec (py:326) computes its iteration count as i - len(mon.trs) + 50. This is negative when the requested record is more than 50 edges in the past, so the 'already sampled' check at py:327 is skipped and py:330 asserts. CHK-031 is the only test that looks back over a 60-edge window (py:1432-1438, the window length comes from the contract's '60 write cycles'). Other tests look back fewer than 50 edges and pass. The failure time matches no waiting at all.
candidates.evidence_against: None found in the files. stop_clock/resume_clock come from nnc_cocotb, which is not in this directory, so their behaviour cannot be confirmed. The early arithmetic failure does not depend on them, though.

candidates.evidence_for: None. No DUT value was compared before the assertion fired.

analyses.rtl_does: At the two failing read edges the DUT still holds the state left by the aborted CHK-031. That test failed at 1354839.78 ns, in the middle of a software reset, just after resume_clock(RCLK). It had 3 accepted pre-reset words, and the request may not yet have reached the read domain. While the read FSM is still in RUN, rd.sv:93,97,117 give o_empty = (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s) = 0 because words were written. This is correct behaviour for a FIFO that holds unread words. Both errors occur before the thr=0 test has reset the DUT: the first read edge of the restarted clock is at 1354839.78 + 2.086 ns = 1354841.87 ns (sim.log:463-465, start delay i_clk_rd 2086 ps), and the second is one 14 ns read period later. analyses.test_does: test_chk_032_threshold_flags (py:1500-1529) builds a new TB (py:1503). TB.__init__ (py:259-274) immediately creates the monitors and a new, empty SB with en=True (py:165). Its on_rd callback (py:206-226) checks every read edge where val(i_rst_n_wr)==val(i_rst_n_rd)==1 (SB.live, py:180-182). tb.init (py:276-288) first starts the clocks, then sets the thresholds, and only then calls reset_dut. So the read edges between test start and the reset assertion are checked against an empty Q while the DUT still holds the previous test's words. Expected o_empty=1 is derived from 'N==0 and P empty' (py:215-218).

candidates.evidence_for: The errors happen 2.09 ns and 14 ns into the test (sim.log:464-465), before the 'CHK-032: S=2 ...' line at 1354972.78 ns that follows init/reset. The SB is enabled from construction (py:165) and does not wait for the test's first reset, so leftover DUT content from the aborted CHK-031 (py:1425-1433 wrote words; the test aborted mid-handshake) is compared with an empty Q. Only the test right after the aborted one fails; thr=1..5 pass. The contract (CHK-005, contract.json:342) assumes Q/P track the DUT from a reset.
candidates.evidence_against: reset_dut is in nnc_cocotb (not provided), so the exact moment the reset is asserted cannot be confirmed from the files. The two error timestamps make it clear that the reset was not yet active.

analyses.spec_says: contract.json:509 (CHK-012): 'o_full and o_full_thr change only in the time step of a rising edge of i_clk_wr, of an assertion of i_rst_n_wr, or of a change of i_rst_n_sw (which the stimulus drives only at i_clk_wr edges). Spec line 167 REQ-SRST-008: 'From the write-clock cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0 ... a write request shall not be accepted. The block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw'. Spec line 176 REQ-SRST-017: 'o_full shall be 1 while the write side is blocked ... o_full_thr ... the values of an empty FIFO'. Spec line 139 REQ-FUNC-010: 'The thresholds are static: they are written once before the FIFO is used'.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:102 `w_wr_blk = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw`, :125 `o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n`, :126 `o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr=='0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr)`. o_full and o_full_thr are therefore combinational in i_rst_n_sw and i_full_thr, as REQ-SRST-008/017 and REQ-FUNC-010 require. o_overflow (:158-163,224) and o_sw_rst_busy (:208-213,225) are posedge/async-reset flops. Every other term (reg_wgray, reg_wbin, w_rgray_s via u_sync_rd_gray, :233-242) changes only at posedge i_clk_wr or on i_rst_n_wr. So between a falling edge and the next rising edge, o_full/o_full_thr can change only if i_rst_n_sw or i_full_thr changes.
analyses.test_does: Checker nnc_chk_wr.sv:48-54 captures o_overflow/busy/full/full_thr at negedge i_clk_wr. :112-114 asserts at the next posedge (rst_q antecedent) that all four equal the captured values. It has no exemption for an i_rst_n_sw change or a threshold change. The stimulus drives i_rst_n_sw right after the falling edge, not at a rising edge: Mon._run fires its Event at FallingEdge (py:137-140), and Writer.loop (py:238-241), TB.w (py:298-303) and full_reset (py:381) write i_rst_n_sw after that event. TB.init (py:281-287) also changes i_full_thr at the start of each test, before reset_dut, while i_rst_n_wr is still 1. Failure distribution in sim.log: almost all fails are in tests that toggle i_rst_n_sw: CHK-017 run_traffic sw=True (sim.log:172-206, 298-307), CHK-023 (1124290..1125060), CHK-025..CHK-029 (1137104..1349836), CHK-030 (1351031, 1351841, 1352921: one per sw pulse), CHK-031 (1354235: the w1 sw=0 pulse), and regression_random sw=True. Tests with i_rst_n_sw=1 throughout (CHK-014/015/018-021, CHK-016 traffic) have no fails except at test starts: 63591000 (CHK-016 pair=0 start at 63582.45 ns, random ft), 1354843000 (thr=0 start, ft 8->0) and 1357015000 (thr=1 start, ft 0->3). Each sw pulse gives one fail, because only the 1->0 edge changes o_full/o_full_thr; at the 0->1 edge busy already holds w_wr_blk=1.

candidates.evidence_for: The contract explicitly allows o_full/o_full_thr to change on an i_rst_n_sw change (contract.json:509), and AF-6.2-06 allows changes from the thresholds. The checker (nnc_chk_wr.sv:112-114) has neither exemption. Its premise that the stimulus drives i_rst_n_sw 'only at i_clk_wr edges', meaning rising edges in the same time step, is broken by the testbench, which drives right after FallingEdge (py:137-140, 238-241, 298-303). The checker therefore samples the pre-change value at the negedge (nnc_chk_wr.sv:49-54). The test-start fails line up with init changing i_full_thr while out of reset (py:281 before py:287), against REQ-FUNC-010's 'written once before the FIFO is used'. All fail timestamps map to an sw pulse or a test start. The flop outputs (o_overflow, busy) cannot change mid-cycle in this RTL.
candidates.evidence_against: Without a waveform, it is not proven that every one of the 254 fails is o_full/o_full_thr and not o_overflow/o_sw_rst_busy. The checker prints only the time (nnc_chk_wr.sv:115). However, those two are plain flops (wr.sv:158-163, 208-213) and CHK-007/008/010 pass.

candidates.evidence_for: o_full/o_full_thr do change between rising edges of i_clk_wr whenever i_rst_n_sw changes, because there is a combinational path (wr.sv:102,125,126).
candidates.evidence_against: That path is required by REQ-SRST-008 ('combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw'), REQ-SRST-018 ('wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0)') and REQ-FUNC-010/018 (combinational flags). CHK-009 (zero-latency block) passes with 0 fails over 6040 hits. Removing the path would break those requirements.

candidates.evidence_for: The contract's parenthetical 'which the stimulus drives only at i_clk_wr edges' does not say rising or falling edge. AF-6.2-06 says LVL-STS flags change 'never between edges except for the effect of the static thresholds' but does not mention i_rst_n_sw. The CHK-012 contract text does not list i_full_thr as an allowed cause.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract does list i_rst_n_sw as an allowed cause for o_full/o_full_thr. The ambiguity concerns only how the checker and stimulus implement that, not what the RTL should do.

analyses.options: Fix test (either option keeps the check's strength for unexplained changes): (1) Drive i_rst_n_sw in the time step of the rising edge of i_clk_wr (e.g., after RisingEdge with a ReadWrite/zero-delay drive, consistent with the contract's 'at i_clk_wr edges'). Or extend the checker to the contract text: compare o_full/o_full_thr against the captured values only when i_rst_n_sw is unchanged since the capture (sample i_rst_n_sw at negedge and at posedge). Keep the strict check for o_overflow and o_sw_rst_busy. (2) In TB.init, set i_full_thr/i_empty_thr only while i_rst_n_wr/i_rst_n_rd are low (assert reset first, then set the thresholds, then release), as REQ-FUNC-010 and the AF-3-17 note in contract.json require. Clarify spec/contract: state whether 'i_clk_wr edges' means rising edges, and add 'static threshold change' to the CHK-012 list as AF-6.2-06 does. No RTL change is indicated. To confirm, print which of the four signals mismatched at each NNC_FAIL CHK-012.

analyses.failure: CHK-013 (assertion): 'o_full_thr consistency for every 4-bit i_full_thr' – 61 fails / 114032 hits, first at 8648000 ps
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524 (CHK-013): '(a) if i_full_thr==0, then o_full_thr=1; (b) if i_full_thr > PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (9..15), then o_full_thr=0; (c) if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy); (d) if o_full=1, i_rst_n_sw=1 and o_sw_rst_busy=0, then o_full_thr == (i_full_thr <= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH).' Spec line 139 REQ-FUNC-010: 'o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr ... it is pessimistic for the full side (it can be larger than the true occupancy) ... a value above the depth makes it never 1.' rules.json:2526 AF-5.4-01 INV-001: 'the number of stored words ... is between 0 and PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH.' Spec line 181 REQ-VER-001: 'For every bit, when the input changes value, the model shall apply a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change ... the model adds 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles ... If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change'. Spec line 1246 TEST-008: with the model, 'no data error; flags never optimistic'.
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:106 `w_full_n = (reg_wgray == (w_rgray_s ^ LPARA_FULL_MSK))`, which is true only when the estimate is exactly DEPTH. :120 `w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s` (4-bit, mod 16). :126 `o_full_thr = ... (w_occ >= i_full_thr)`. For any synchronized pointer that is a real past read-pointer value, w_occ is in 0..8, and clauses (a)-(d) hold identically: occ>=8 <=> occ==8 <=> w_full_n; occ<=8<thr for thr>8. The clauses can fail only if w_occ is in 9..15, i.e., w_rbin_s is not a valid recent read-pointer value. The sim model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 (instantiated per bit by m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv:46-56) delays each bit independently by 0..2 extra destination cycles (:158-177). When the source Gray pointer changes two or more times within that window (e.g., read clock faster than or close to the write clock), different bits are shown from different moments. Example: read pointer 1->2->3 = Gray 0001->0011->0010. If the bit1 rise is delayed and the bit0 fall is not, the write domain sees 0000 (=0), which is behind any value it saw before. Then w_occ = wbin - 0 can be 9: o_full_thr=1 (>=8) while w_full_n=0, so clause (c) fails. This is a hypothesis; no waveform is available to confirm it.
analyses.test_does: The checker nnc_chk_wr.sv:119-125 implements (a)-(d) at every posedge i_clk_wr with i_rst_n_wr=1, as a pure combinational consistency check. Fails appear in tests where the read pointer can change two or more times within about 3 write cycles: CHK-014 per=1 (write 14 ns / read 6 ns, ft=8; fails 8648000, 9656000, 10734000; py:688-701), CHK-016 pair=1 (10/10.3) and pair=4 (23/10) (sim.log:117-139, 153-171), CHK-017 and CHK-018 (10/14, ft=8), CHK-029 pair=2 (23/10) and regression_random. There are none in CHK-032 or the directed isolated-access tests. The run has the metastability model on (sim.log:27 '+AFIFO_MSYNC_SEED=1 +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1'; results.json:279-295). Expected values come from the contract formula, not from a model of the synchronizer.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model does exactly what REQ-VER-001 / AF-10.6.4-01 ('Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent ... extra delay of 0, 1, or 2') specify (cell_sync.sv:149-182). Per-bit independent delays of up to 2 cycles let the synchronized Gray vector show combinations that never existed at the source when the source steps faster than the delay window. That breaks the single-bit-change property that REQ-FUNC-010 ('a value above the depth makes it never 1'), INV-001 and TEST-008 ('flags never optimistic') rely on. The spec's own demonstration spaces pointer steps 'six source cycles apart' (spec:653), so the case was never shown. The spec is internally inconsistent: the model it mandates can produce occupancy estimates outside 0..DEPTH.
candidates.evidence_against: Not confirmed by waveform. An equivalent model-off run (+AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 or VLSIT_SYNTHESIS) is not available here. CHK-005/CHK-006 report 0 fails, so in this seed the out-of-range estimates did not cause an observed data error.

candidates.evidence_for: The simulation model is part of the delivered RTL (rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv) and is meant to model metastability (spec:653 'It models the extra delay caused by metastability'). Physical 2-FF synchronizers on a Gray bus cannot show 'old value of an earlier-changed bit with new value of a later-changed bit'. A model that does is unrealistic, and could be changed, e.g., to delay the vector coherently or cap the extra delay so later changes cannot overtake earlier ones. The functional RTL (wr.sv:106,120,126) could also be considered fragile because occupancy is not range-limited.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows the letter of REQ-VER-001. The functional flag logic follows REQ-FUNC-010 exactly and is self-consistent for any legal (coherent) pointer. Changing the model's behaviour requires a spec decision first.

candidates.evidence_for: The check assumes the write-domain estimate is always within 0..DEPTH, which the mandated model does not guarantee.
candidates.evidence_against: The check quotes REQ-FUNC-010 / DEC-006 faithfully, and the invariant it tests is a legitimate design property (INV-001, TEST-008 'flags never optimistic'). It is not a testbench mistake, and weakening it is not appropriate.

analyses.options: First, confirm the hypothesis: rerun the same tests with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 (and/or VLSIT_SYNTHESIS). If CHK-013 fails disappear, the model is the cause. Add a debug monitor that flags when w_rgray_s changes by more than one bit per write edge or moves backwards, and print i_full_thr, o_full and o_full_thr at each NNC_FAIL. Clarify spec (designer decision): either (1) require the metastability model to keep the synchronized Gray vector coherent, e.g., a bit's pending change may not be overtaken by a later change of another bit, or the extra delay is drawn once per vector change; then change cell_sync.sv:149-182, which needs sync-level context (m_vlsit_afifo_sync), or (2) keep per-bit independence and state that it only applies to isolated changes, constraining the stimulus to that case, which would also restrict CHK-016/029 ratios. Fix RTL only after the spec decision: implement the coherent model. Do not weaken CHK-013; it encodes REQ-FUNC-010.

analyses.failure: CHK-003 (assertion): 'o_empty_thr consistency for every 4-bit i_empty_thr' – 45 fails / 100586 hits, first at 231868000 ps
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:287 (CHK-003): 'At every rising edge of i_clk_rd, and while i_rst_n_rd=0: (a) if o_empty=1, then o_empty_thr=1 ... (b) If i_empty_thr >= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_empty_thr=1. (c) If i_empty_thr==0, then o_empty_thr == o_empty.' Spec line 139 REQ-FUNC-010: 'o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr ... it is pessimistic ... for the empty side (it can be smaller).' rules.json:3240 AF-6.2-21: 'Occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr'. rules.json:2526 AF-5.4-01 INV-001 (occupancy 0..DEPTH). Spec line 181 REQ-VER-001: per-bit independent random extra latency 0..2, with replacement of pending changes.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:97 `w_empty_n = (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s)`, :112 `w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin` (4-bit mod 16), :117 `o_empty = w_rd_blk | w_empty_n`, :118 `o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr)`. Clauses (a) and (c) hold for any input values: empty_n <=> occ==0 <=> occ<=0, and blocked forces both to 1. So the fails must come from clause (b): i_empty_thr in 8..14 with w_occ > i_empty_thr, i.e., a read-domain estimate of 9..15. That happens only if w_wgray_s is not a coherent recent write-pointer value. The per-bit model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182) can produce such a value when the write pointer steps two or more times within the 0..2-cycle extra window. 'Ahead' example: 2->3->4 = 0011->0010->0110; showing only the bit2 rise gives 0111 = 5. 'Behind' example: a value below reg_rbin gives a negative estimate that wraps to 15 and also drives o_empty=0. This is a hypothesis without a waveform.
analyses.test_does: The checker nnc_chk_rd.sv:73-78 asserts (a)-(c) at every posedge i_clk_rd, with no disable. Fails occur only where the write side is faster than the read side and i_empty_thr is random: CHK-016 pair=2 (10/23 ns) 231868000..343326000 (sim.log:140-152), CHK-029 pair=1 (10/23) 1189034000..1222246000 (sim.log:353-382), and regression_random (default 10/14, random et, py:1537) 1370422000.. (sim.log:571-675). There are none in pair=0/1/3/4/5 of CHK-016, which have different random thresholds and ratios. The metastability model is on for the whole run (sim.log:27). Expected values come from the contract formula.

candidates.evidence_for: Given the RTL equations, only clause (b) can fail, and only with a read-domain estimate above DEPTH. The model behaviour that allows this is exactly what REQ-VER-001 / AF-10.6.4-01 mandate ('Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent'). That conflicts with REQ-FUNC-010 (estimate 'can be smaller' on the empty side, i.e. pessimistic), INV-001 and TEST-008 ('flags never optimistic'). The failures cluster at the fast-write/slow-read ratios, where several write-pointer steps fall within one delay window. This is the mirror of CHK-013, which clusters at fast-read ratios.
candidates.evidence_against: There is no waveform or model-off rerun to confirm. CHK-005/006 show 0 fails, so no data error was observed in this seed. It cannot be excluded that a few fails come from another source (e.g., a one-domain hardware reset in regression_random leaving the pointers mismatched).

candidates.evidence_for: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:158-177 lets a later change on one bit appear before an earlier pending change on another bit. A physical synchronizer on a Gray bus cannot do this, so the delivered simulation model is unrealistic and makes the read side see more words than were written. rd.sv:112/118 do not range-limit the estimate.
candidates.evidence_against: The model is literally compliant with REQ-VER-001. The flag logic follows REQ-FUNC-010 and is consistent for any coherent pointer. A model change needs a spec decision.

candidates.evidence_for: The checker assumes the read-domain estimate never exceeds DEPTH, which the mandated model does not guarantee.
candidates.evidence_against: The check is a direct reading of REQ-FUNC-010/DEC-006 and INV-001 and is a valid design property. The stimulus (random traffic, static thresholds set before release) is legal. Weakening the check is not appropriate.

Print i_empty_thr, o_empty, o_empty_thr and the internal w_wgray_s/reg_rgray at each NNC_FAIL CHK-003, and add a debug check that w_wgray_s changes by at most one bit per read edge and never moves backwards. Clarify spec: decide whether the REQ-VER-001 model must keep multi-bit Gray coherence; this is the same decision as for CHK-013. Fix RTL after that decision: make cell_sync/sync apply the delay so a later bit change cannot overtake an earlier pending one, or apply one delay per vector change. Then rerun all seeds and check that CHK-003, CHK-013 and CHK-005/006 stay clean. Do not weaken CHK-003.
